issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor declaration in the template header uses parameter types 'long i_width, long i_height' but the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp defines the constructor with parameter types 'int p_width, int p_height'. This mismatch between declaration and definition will cause a linker/compilation error and confuses students about the intended constructor signature. The solution repository header uses 'int' (matching the implementation), indicating the template header's 'long' is unintended.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration and definition use the same parameter types. Update example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the template repository to declare 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);' (matching the .cpp implementation), or alternatively change the Bitmap24.cpp definition to use 'long' for the parameters. Prefer matching the solution (use 'int') to preserve consistency.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor is represented with inconsistent signatures across artifacts. In the template repository header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the constructor is declared as 'Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height);' while the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines 'Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height)'. The solution repository consistently uses 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)'. This mismatch (long vs int and header vs implementation) makes it unclear which constructor signature students should follow, can cause compilation errors in the template, and creates unnecessary cognitive load when mapping the class declaration to its implementation and to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent constructor signature across header and implementation in both template and solution. For example, change the template header declaration to 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);' to match the implementation and the solution. Alternatively, change the implementation to use 'long' everywhere if that is intended. Ensure header and .cpp signatures match so students can unambiguously map declaration to implementation.
